newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kinnock offers help on French truck strike.
newsitem.headline: Kinnock offers help on French truck strike.

text.p: European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Monday he was in touch with French authorities to see if there was anything the European Commission could do to help resolve the French truckers strike.
Kinnock, in a statement read to reporters by a Commission spokesman, said the Commission could not do much under EU law to to intervene directly in a national strike.
"(It) notes, however...that some of the concerns that have been expressed by the French truckers involve working conditions such as driving time that are the subject of EU regulations," he said.

Kinnock said the Commission was in the process of reviewing whether to strengthen EU rules covering truck drivers, citing a proposal to introduce high-technology devices into cabs to ensure that they do not exceed daily limits on driving hours.
That proposal is set to be discussed by the Transport Council next month, a Commission official said.

The Commission is also considering whether to propose that the EU's Working Time Directive, 93/104/EC, which covers working hours and rest periods, be applied to truck drivers, who are now excluded, officials noted.
The Commission is drafting a White Paper on that question following the European Court of Justice ruling earlier this month upholding the directive's legality.
The French strikers, who have set up roadblocks across the country, are demanding higher wages, shorter hours and retirement at age 55 rather than 60.

"Mr Kinnock and his staff are in direct contact with the French authorities to see what the Commission can do and of course if it can do something, it will not hesitate to do it to help resolve this difficult situation," Kinnock's statement said.
